title: Construction Practice Certificates from 1 March 2027: Who Needs One?
desc: From 1 March 2027, Law 24/2026/QH16 amends Article 88 of the Construction Law, dropping certificates for cost management leads. Which roles still need one.
summary: Law 24/2026/QH16 amends Clauses 1 and 2, Article 88 of the Construction Law 2025 from 1 March 2027; this article compares the list of positions that must hold a practice certificate before and after that date.
body: p

On 24 August 2026, the National Assembly passed Law No. 24/2026/QH16. Besides its investment content, Clause 4, Article 2 of this Law amends Clauses 1 and 2 of Article 88 of the Construction Law 2025 - the article that sets out who must hold a construction activity practice certificate. The new rule applies from 1 March 2027 (Clause 1, Article 2 of Law 24/2026/QH16).
h2
1. Positions that must hold a practice certificate: before and after 1 March 2027
p

Until the end of 28 February 2027, under Clause 1, Article 88 of the Construction Law 2025, a practice certificate is required to act as: head or lead of urban and rural planning design; head of construction survey; head or lead of construction design or design verification; construction supervisor; lead for determining, verifying and managing construction investment costs.
p
From 1 March 2027, Clause 1, Article 88 is rewritten and lists only:
ul
Head or lead in preparing urban and rural planning;
Head of construction survey;
Head or lead of construction design or design verification;
Construction supervisor.
p

Certificates are still divided into grade I, grade II and grade III. The position of lead for determining, verifying and managing construction investment costs is no longer on the list requiring a certificate (Clause 4, Article 2 of Law 24/2026/QH16).
h2
2. Positions that only need to meet capacity conditions
p

The current Clause 2, Article 88 requires the site chief commander, the lead for construction inspection and the project management director to meet professional capacity and experience conditions. From 1 March 2027, Clause 2 names only the construction investment project management director and the site chief commander.
p

The conditions for these two positions are in Article 38 of Decree 212/2026/ND-CP. For example, a grade III site chief commander needs 2 years of experience (university level) or 3 years (college level) and must have taken part in carrying out the corresponding part of 1 work of grade III or above or 2 works of grade IV.
h2
3. Fields in which practice certificates are currently issued
p

Under Article 28 of Decree 212/2026/ND-CP, practice certificates are issued in these fields: construction survey (topographic, engineering geological); urban and rural planning; construction design (architectural design follows architecture law, construction works design, mechanical and electrical design); construction supervision.
p

Where a dossier was submitted before Decree 212/2026/ND-CP took effect asking for a Project Management or Construction Cost Estimating certificate, the competent authority does not issue these certificates (Clause 2, Article 55).
h2
4. A point to note: independent practice
p

Article 90 of the Construction Law 2025 provides that individuals practising independently in survey; design and design verification; construction supervision; and determining, verifying and managing construction investment costs must hold a practice certificate. Law 24/2026/QH16 amends only Clauses 1 and 2 of Article 88, not Article 90. Independent practitioners in cost matters should ask the Department of Construction for specific guidance after 1 March 2027.
h2
5. What should owners check?
ul

The lead designer, the design verifier and the construction supervisor of your house must hold appropriate certificates; the investor is responsible for the choice of those engaged (Clause 5, Article 88).

No certificate is required for designing or supervising finishing work such as plastering, tiling, painting, door installation and work that does not affect the load-bearing structure (Point c, Clause 3, Article 27 of Decree 212/2026/ND-CP).

Certificates issued under the Construction Law 2014 continue to be used within the field and scope stated on the certificate until they expire (Clause 5, Article 55); newly issued certificates are valid for 10 years (Clause 5, Article 27).
Construction companies do not need a capacity certificate but publicly declare their capacity on the web portal of the Ministry of Construction (Clause 6, Article 88).
p
See also: Individual construction activity practice certificates 2026 and Do construction enterprises still need a capacity certificate?
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace the legal texts. Law 24/2026/QH16, amending Clauses 1 and 2, Article 88 of the Construction Law 2025, takes effect on 1 March 2027. According to the library list, Resolution 66.18/2026/NQ-CP on cutting business conditions applies until the end of 28 February 2027 but its full text is not in the library. Decree 212/2026/ND-CP may be amended to conform to the new Law; ask the Department of Construction before preparing a dossier.
